Phrase functions

Source: R/phrases.R
phrases.Rd

Wording that arithmetic fixes (rule 3.5). Each returns a weft_text. They print English words, so under a lang weft does not ship they are a construct error (rule 1.6.8).

Usage

of_n(k, n, singular, plural)

about(x, to = 1/2, tolerance = NULL)

ci(
  est,
  lo,
  hi,
  level = NULL,
  digits = NULL,
  sigfig = NULL,
  plus = FALSE,
  pct = FALSE,
  short = NULL
)

pm(est, se, digits = NULL, sigfig = NULL)

clamp(x, floor = NULL, ceiling = NULL)

Arguments

k, n

Whole numbers, 0 <= k <= n, n > 0.

singular, plural

The noun, in each form.

x

A number.

to

The target of about().

tolerance

The largest distance from to that about() accepts.

est, lo, hi, se

Numbers.

level

The confidence level of ci(), as a proportion.

digits, sigfig

Decimal places or significant figures, as for fmt_num().

plus, pct, short

TRUE or FALSE (short also NULL) for ci(); see above.

floor, ceiling

The bounds of clamp(); NULL for none.

Value

A weft_text.

Details

  • of_n(k, n, singular, plural) prints "none of the 4 sites", "the only site", "both sites", "all 5 sites" or "3 of the 7 sites". Its number is k, so an n span after it agrees with it (rule 3.5.2).

  • about(x, to, tolerance) prints "nearly half", "just over half" or "half". to is one of 1/4, 1/3, 1/2, 2/3 and 3/4. x and to are compared as percentages rounded to whole numbers. An x further than tolerance from to is a value error, because the sentence would be false. The default tolerance is the setting about_tolerance (0.05).

  • ci(est, lo, hi, level, digits, sigfig, plus, pct, short) prints "2.1 (95% CI 1.3 to 2.9)". The default level is the setting ci_level (0.95). plus = TRUE signs the three numbers as .plus does; pct = TRUE prints each as .pct does; short = TRUE (default: the setting ci_short) leaves out "95% CI", and a level given with the short form is a weft_value_error.

  • pm(est, se, digits, sigfig) prints the estimate, a plus-minus sign and the standard error. When digits and sigfig are not given and a number of ci() or pm() that is not zero prints as zero, one warned check of kind "printed as zero" is recorded for the call, as for fmt_num().

  • clamp(x, floor, ceiling) prints the value as .num does inside the bounds, and "< floor" or "> ceiling" outside, with the relation of the printed record set (rule 3.5.4).

Given a quantity (a units value, see u()), of_n() and about() use its number and print no unit: they print words. ci(), pm() and clamp() do not take a quantity that has a unit (rule 4.4.8) and stop with a weft_value_error; pass the numbers, or format the parts with fmt_num(); so does a formatter's text that carries a unit. Given two quantities, of_n() converts n to the unit of k, and about() converts x to the unit of to; units that do not convert are a weft_value_error. A ratio, which has no unit left, is a number.

Examples

of_n(3, 7, "site", "sites")
#> <weft_text>
#> [1] "3 of the 7 sites"
about(0.49)
#> <weft_text>
#> [1] "nearly half"
ci(2.1, 1.3, 2.9)
#> <weft_text>
#> [1] "2.1 (95% CI 1.3 to 2.9)"
pm(2.1, 0.3)
#> <weft_text>
#> [1] "2.1 ± 0.3"
clamp(150, ceiling = 99)
#> <weft_text>
#> [1] "> 99"
